title: Using super with overridden methods
answer: Inside a subclass, `super.method()` explicitly invokes the accessible superclass implementation of that method instead of performing normal virtual dispatch to the current object's override. This lets an override extend or reuse parent behavior while still adding child-specific work. `super` is statically tied to the immediate superclass context; it is not a separate object and cannot be used to select arbitrary ancestors.
